set.n: Fort St. Joseph gold: well cache and river-bank cache above the dam, Niles (legend; bank cache rumoured found c.1850s)
set.v: Gold in the fort well and on the river bank (no figure)
set.st: Old Niles people said the French fort just above the dam (Fort St. Joseph) was massacred by Indians, and that gold was thrown into the fort's well and more buried on the river bank. The late Ransom Dopp (a stage driver in 1848, later owner of about 1,500 acres in Wayne Twp, Cass Co) was rumoured to have found the bank cache: he was seen digging on the river bank, stopped suddenly, and then bought a large tract. The Dowagiac Republican, answering, said his neighbours doubted it. The Niles editor had heard the tale more than 50 years earlier from the Indian Bertrand. In Dec 1898, answering the Chicago Chronicle's Bertrand story, the Niles Daily Star had already noted that locals told of a large sum buried 'just above the dam in this city' in the French and Indian war.
set.t: Oral legend first printed 1899; the 'bank cache found' part rests on a rumour his neighbours denied. The fort site is a registered archaeological site: look only, never dig; urban riverbank. The dam: the 1889 Sanborn map shows it about 3/4 mile south of Main St between the pulp and paper mills, and the LiDAR water surface steps up about 4 m there; 'just above the dam' is the stretch upstream (south) of it.
set.warn: Registered archaeological site and urban riverbank: look only, never dig.
set.tovw: One 1899 account (two Niles papers) + 1898 aside; legend
pinev: 1889 Sanborn, Niles, sheet 6: DAM across the St Joseph between the Michigan Wood Pulp Co. and the Ohio Paper Co. mills, '3/4 mile S. of Main St'.

2015 1 m LiDAR: the flattened river surface steps up about 4.2 m (194.7 m to 198.9 m) at about 41.8175, -86.2588, which is the dam; pin about 150 m upstream of it. Moved from a pin about 2 km north, off the river.
The 1899 account places the fort 'just above the dam', matching the Fort St. Joseph site on the E bank upstream of the dam; pin unchanged.

src: Niles Weekly Mirror, 21 Jun 1899, p. 4, 'Ransom Dopp' (Newspapers.com 1064542190); same account in Niles Daily Star, 21 Jun 1899 (1019705180), with the Dowagiac Republican's reply
